signals.title: Adventure motorcycles continue to steer the UK’s positive sales numbers
signals.summary: Adventure motorcycle registrations grew by 41 per cent in July compared to the same month in 2025. 2026 has so far been a strong year for motorcycle sales in the UK, which continued in July, according to the latest statistics provided by the Motorcycle Industry Association (MCIA). The adventure segment has played a key role in the ongoing growth month-to-month vs 2025, and that was also the case in July. Adventure motorcycle registrations were up by a staggering 41.8 per cent compared to the same month in 2025. Year-to-date, adventure motorcycle sales are also holding strong, with an overall increase of 26.2 per cent. The naked motorcycle segment also flourished in July, with registrations growing by 24.5 per cent compared with July 2025. Not far behind that was the touring segment, with monthly registrations growing by 18.2 per cent. Year-to-date registrations for the entire motorcycle segment have grown by 16.1 per cent, while YTD scooter sales are up by 15.4 per cent. In terms of individual models, the best-performing bike in July 2026 was the Honda CB125F, which sold 185 units in the naked category. That was then followed by the CB1000GT which sold 141 units, while third place went the way of the GB350S, meaning Honda finished the month with the three best-selling motorcycles. signals.summary: Superbike Factory customers and former staff have created online groups to share information following the motorcycle dealer's administration. The collapse of Superbike Factory has prompted affected customers and staff to organise themselves online, with Reddit and WhatsApp groups now being used to share information about the administration and help people work out what to do next. The groups have been set up in the aftermath of Superbike Factory entering administration on 20 July 2026, when the company's appointed administrators confirmed that the business had ceased trading with immediate effect. One customer who contacted Visordown said they initially discovered the community through a discussion on a legal advice forum on Reddit. The discussion has since become a focal point for people attempting to share experiences and information following the dealer's collapse. The Reddit discussion includes contributions from people affected in different ways, while a separate WhatsApp group has been established specifically for Superbike Factory customers and staff. The WhatsApp group describes itself as being for “Affected Customers and staff”, with the intention of bringing people together to exchange information as the administration progresses. signals.title: Ducati bidder wants MV Agusta too... and Triumph out of Moto2!
signals.summary: The group behind a €2.5bn bid for Ducati has outlined what it would do if the deal goes through, including replacing Triumph in Moto2 and making the entire operation Italian! Patritalia has reiterated its bid to buy Ducati from the Audi/Volkswagen Group, claiming that its €2.5bn offer remains on the table indefinitely and outlining what it would do if it gets its hands on the Bologna-based manufacturer. And if it’s CEO and founder is to be believed, it isn't stopping at Ducati. The Italian group says MV Agusta is also among its targets, with the stated aim of returning both brands, and other unnamed Italian companies, to Italian ownership. Patritalia says this is central to its founding philosophy and that Ducati and MV Agusta are of interest specifically because they are currently foreign-owned. Quite how far that philosophy would extend is where things get interesting. Most notably, it says its companies would be "always and only" made up of Italians, regardless of the skills foreign employees might bring. signals.title: Ducati secures major research and development investment fund
signals.summary: Despite ongoing rumours of the company potentially being sold, Ducati is set to strengthen its research and development capabilities through a new €121m investment fund. Ducati has secured a €121m (around £104m) investment fund to strengthen competitiveness, innovation and growth through its new project, ‘Ducati Raise the Bar’. Ducati says the new programme will focus heavily on the company’s R&D (Research and Development) sector, as well as technical innovation. The Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy authorised the new agreement, according to Ducati, which includes a non-repayable grant from the Ministry of €33.5m, which converts to roughly £28.7m. This means that just over 25 per cent of the programme will be funded by the government ministry. What all of this indicates is that Ducati, despite ongoing rumours of the company being sold by current owners Volkswagen AG, is set to invest heavily in the development of future motorcycles, its racing programmes, and the company’s wider business operations. At the heart of Ducati’s new programme will be “industrial research and experimental development”, with the Bologna-based company allocating €99m (around £85m) to this particular sector. Alongside the research and development plan, which Ducati hopes will strengthen its position as one of the biggest motorcycle brands in the world, the programme is also about contributing to local areas in Italy. signals.title: Norton has a surprising plan to take on Ducati, BMW and Triumph
signals.summary: Norton teams up with Foster + Partners to create a new global dealership concept as it pushes towards a worldwide network of more than 200 retailers. Norton is betting that selling premium motorcycles shouldn't feel like buying any other bike. Instead of another dealership refresh with swanky signage and posh furniture, the British brand has teamed up with world-renowned architecture firm Foster + Partners to create a completely new retail experience. You may also like to read our Norton Manx R review . The new showroom design, which is part of Norton’s 200-dealer global expansion, is intended to change how customers experience the brand, with motorcycles displayed more like fine art than machines lined up on a sales floor. Norton says the concept combines gallery-style displays with dedicated areas where customers can configure their bikes, explore the engineering behind them and interact with digital displays. If the name Foster + Partners sounds familiar, there's a good reason. The British architecture firm, founded by Sir Norman Foster, is responsible for some of the world's most recognisable buildings, including London's Gherkin skyscraper, Apple's headquarters in California and Wembley Stadium's redevelopment. Bringing a firm with that pedigree into motorcycle retail is an unusual move, and shows Norton is aiming to position itself firmly at the premium end of the market. signals.title: Motorcyclists now have an official voice inside the European Parliament
signals.summary: The European Parliament has launched a new cross-party Motorcycling MEP Club, giving riders a dedicated voice as new transport and environmental laws continue to emerge. The European Parliament now has an official group dedicated to motorcycles, with a new cross-party Motorcycling MEP Club launching in Brussels as the industry looks to strengthen its influence over future transport legislation. The new group was formally established on 1 July, bringing together Members of the European Parliament from across the political spectrum with the aim of ensuring motorcycles, scooters and mopeds continue to be considered when new mobility, environmental and road safety policies are developed. The club elected Andreas Glück as its first Chair, with Matej Tonin, Bernd Lange and Nora Junco serving as Vice-Chairs. To mark the launch, members joined the European Association of Motorcycle Manufacturers (ACEM) for its annual Summer Ride, completing a 50km route through and around Brussels before attending an evening reception. The event also marked the first public appearance of Markus Flasch in his new role as ACEM President, having taken over the position following the association's General Assembly in Munich. While the ride itself was largely symbolic, the formation of the Motorcycling MEP Club could prove significant. signals.title: LiveWire shares surge above $2 just days after penny stock warning
signals.summary: Harley-Davidson-backed LiveWire was warned its shares had slipped below NYSE listing requirements, but within days the stock had climbed back above $2. It looked like another grim chapter in LiveWire's difficult few years, but just days after being warned it had effectively become a penny stock, the electric motorcycle firm saw its share price bounce back above the crucial $2 mark. The Harley-Davidson-backed EV brand confirmed it received a notice from the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) on July 23 after its shares had averaged below $1 over a consecutive 30 trading-day period, putting it in breach of the exchange's continued listing rules. While that sounds serious, the notice doesn't mean LiveWire is about to disappear from the NYSE, and the company has up to six months to restore compliance. While "penny stock" sounds like a throwaway label, it carries real consequences. Companies with shares trading at very low prices are often seen as higher-risk investments, something that can put off larger investors and pile further pressure on the share price. For firms listed on the NYSE, staying above $1 is also important because falling below that level for a sustained period can eventually lead to delisting if the issue isn't fixed. Under NYSE rules, LiveWire has ten business days to tell the exchange how it intends to fix the problem. signals.title: Ducati takeover bidder's CEO takes to social media to back sale claims
signals.summary: Ducati's sale rumours have taken another twist, with an Italian investment company confirming the news, while the firm's CEO publicly backed the claim on social media. For more than a year, rumours that Ducati could be sold by Volkswagen Group have come and gone, fuelled by reports of wider restructuring within the German automotive giant rather than anything direct from the Borgo Panigale. Now, for the first time, a company has publicly confirmed it has made an offer to buy the Italian manufacturer. Speaking to RideApart, Massimo Ros, founder of Italian investment company Patritalia S.p.A., said his company had formally approached Volkswagen with a bid to acquire Ducati Motor Holding in its entirety. "I can confirm that the rumours are well founded. Patritalia S.p.A has formally expressed its interest and is fully prepared to acquire 100% of Ducati Motor Holding S.p.A." According to Ros, Patritalia was founded with the aim of returning iconic Italian companies to Italian ownership. "The sole mission I set behind the creation of Patritalia is to 'bring back home' our Italian companies and iconic Italian brands that are currently under foreign ownership and bring them back under Italian control. Our objective is to promote a form of industrial repossession, allowing these historic brands to once again be guided by Italian vision, culture, creativity, with the goal of restoring the soul of the Italian entrepreneurial spirit." signals.title: Honda may have predicted the EU's next move on motorcycle sustainability
signals.summary: The EU has made recycled plastics mandatory for new cars from 2032. Motorcycles are exempt for now, but Honda's early adoption suggests the industry may already know what’s coming. When Honda announced last year that it was expanding the use of recycled plastics and bio-based materials across its motorcycle range, it looked like either another step on the road towards a more sustainable future, or a brand going above and beyond to seem more green. Fast forward to today, though, and that decision suddenly looks rather more significant. The European Union has now formally adopted its new End-of-Life Vehicle Regulation (ELVR), introducing mandatory recycled plastic content for all newly type-approved passenger cars and vans from 2032. Motorcycles aren't included in the legislation, but history suggests bike manufacturers would be unwise to assume they'll stay outside the scope forever. The regulation, published in the Official Journal of the European Union on July 24 and coming into force on August 13, is one of the biggest shake-ups of automotive manufacturing in decades. From September 1, 2032, every newly type-approved passenger car and van sold in the EU will need to contain at least 15 per cent recycled plastic, with that figure rising to 25 per cent for newly type-approved vehicles from September 1, 2036. signals.title: Before manufacturers discovered influencers, Triumph made this viral masterpiece
signals.summary: Motorcycle marketing has changed beyond recognition, but this classic Triumph Rocket III video remains as absolute comedy gold. Before social media algorithms, before influencers, before every bike launch needed a cinematic drone shot and someone dramatically staring into the middle distance, Triumph quietly released what might still be the funniest motorcycle video ever made. You may also like to read our Triumph Rocket 3 review . Originally uploaded back in 2007 to promote the then-new Rocket III Classic, the spoof factory documentary has somehow aged better than plenty of modern motorcycle marketing campaigns. Presented as a serious behind-the-scenes look inside Triumph's production line, the video quickly descends into the kind of glorious nonsense that has us waiting for Basil Fawlty to appear. Engines are tested to the sound of banjo music "for safety purposes", workers carefully harvest chrome from fields, and the bike's legendary handling is apparently thanks to "argument juice" extracted from the female brain. And as for the 2,300cc engine which is apparently “grown from embryo engines, germinated in a nutrient-rich sludge medium” and then left in a cupboard by the photocopiers. It's exactly the sort of deadpan British humour that made me fall in love with British comedy back in the 80s and 90s. From The Fast Show to Vic and Bob’s Big Night Out, this piece of comedic artwork was a perfect snapshot of where UK comedy was at the time. We first shared the clip on Visord
